text: The prompt that `DefaultSystemPromptBuilder().build_system_prompt` returns contains an ambiguous-questions section for every tool list, including the empty list and the full list with both save tools enabled (`run_sql`, `emit_chart`, `emit_text`, `search_saved_correct_tool_uses`, `save_question_tool_args`, `save_text_memory`). The section names no tool and states at minimum these clauses: (1) ask a clarifying question instead of answering when the question allows more than one reading, the readings count different records, a different period, or a different measure or calculation, and the choice is not settled, with whether partially paid orders count toward revenue, whether the order date or the invoice date defines the period, which of several people a name refers to, and whether revenue includes shipping and tax as examples; such a choice counts as material without first measuring the difference, and being unsure which reading is meant is a reason to ask; (2) a choice is settled when the question, an earlier turn of the conversation, a memory note in the context naming the meaning to use, or a saved question-and-SQL pair seen for the question says or shows which reading is meant; a saved pair settles it to the reading its SQL uses, and a memory note saying a term has more than one meaning marks that choice as open, which the question, an earlier turn, a note naming the meaning to use, a saved pair or a reply that picks a reading still settles; (3) a choice stays open until settled: a reply that picks a reading, or asks to see several readings, settles it, and a reply that picks none, such as "whatever you think", leaves it open; while a choice the current question depends on stays open, ask again on each turn, offering the readings as choices; a new question that does not depend on an open choice is handled on its own terms; (4) otherwise answer directly: a question with one reasonable reading, or a choice whose readings count the same records, period and measure or differ only in presentation (sort order, chart type, labels, rounding), never needs a question; (5) the question is the agent's whole written reply for that turn: short, naming the readings in business words without table or column names, and stating no result for any reading; on that turn this overrides the rule to state a one-row result's values, because a lookup's rows are already shown above the question; (6) run a lookup query before asking only when it is needed to know the readings, and when many records match, ask for a detail that narrows them; (7) ask at most one question per turn, covering every open choice the current question depends on; (8) on every turn, never state a result computed on a reading of an unsettled choice that changes the numbers.

When `search_saved_correct_tool_uses` is in the tool list, the prompt's memory instructions require calling it before asking a clarifying question as well as before executing `run_sql` or `emit_chart`. When it is not in the tool list, the prompt carries no instruction to search memory before asking.

The `query_database` tool description returned by the server's `list_tools` tells the calling assistant that when a result is a clarifying question rather than an answer, it asks the user that question, or uses the answer the user's earlier messages already give, and then calls `query_database` again with that answer as `question` and the `conversation_id` the result returned.

An automated test calls the registered `query_database` MCP tool twice, with a scripted model behind a real agent. On turn one the scripted model replies with only a clarifying question: the result is not an error, its text begins with that question, and it carries a conversation id. On turn two, sent with that id and a reply, the request the model receives holds, in order, the original question, the clarifying question and the reply. The system prompt the model receives on both turns contains the ambiguous-questions section.

`docs/external/managing-memory.md` explains how a deployment marks a known ambiguity with a free-form note that states, as a fact, that a term has more than one meaning, and how a note naming the meaning to use, or a saved question-and-SQL pair for the question that the assistant's memory search finds, can stop the question. It gives a made-up example of each, and says a note reaches the assistant only on a turn whose message the automatic background context retrieves it for. Its "Verifying Memory After an Import" section says a golden question that leaves such a choice open may get a clarifying question instead of SQL, reported as ERROR when no query ran and compared using the lookup query's SQL when one ran, and tells operators to state the choice in golden questions.

No sentence in `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` or in the docstrings and comments of `src/sqllens/tools/_format.py` says the agent's own clarifying question is expressed as an interactive component (a prompt placeholder, buttons or an alert) or reaches the caller through `render_interactive`. `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` describes `render_interactive` as rendering interactive components and the agent's clarifying question as arriving as answer-marked text. The sites are found by a case-insensitive search of those two files for "clarifying question" and "interactive affordance".

The change leaves `src/sqllens/eval/` unchanged: a `verify-memory` case where the agent asks instead of answering is reported ERROR when no query ran, and is compared using the lookup query as its actual SQL when a lookup ran first. The change leaves the block building in `components_to_blocks` unchanged, so rows returned by a lookup against the data run before the question appear as a block before the question. The change adds no `_meta` channel or flag marking a clarifying-question turn, so whether the calling assistant relays the question depends on it following the tool description. The change leaves `src/sqllens/agent/core/enhancer/default.py` unchanged, so a note the context enhancer does not retrieve for the current turn's message does not reach the agent through the memory context. The change adds no code that forces the memory search before a question, so a model that skips the search, or a search with the agent's own wording that misses a saved pair, can still ask on a question a saved pair would settle. The change adds no configuration field, no MCP tool and no agent tool.
